---
title: "Image viewer"
---

Askr supplies one interactive image viewer in two modes: inspect an image
directly in the article, or open a floating viewer from an image or button.
SVG, PNG and JPEG share the same pan-and-zoom controls. No image service,
third-party viewer or CDN is required.

## Images and opt-outs

Independent figures and standalone images open the floating viewer by default:

```markdown
![Layout](images/layout.svg){#fig-layout}
```

Inline prose images and images with an existing navigation link keep their
normal treatment. `.lightbox` explicitly enables an image;
`.nolightbox` excludes it. `lightbox: false` disables interaction for the page.
Do not use viewer shortcodes on a disabled page or target an excluded image.
Rendering reports the conflict instead of producing unusable controls.

## Open with a button

Open an existing figure without duplicating its image or caption:

```markdown
![Layout](images/layout.png){#fig-layout}

{{{< askr-image-view target="fig-layout" label="View image" >}}}
```

Or show only a button:

```markdown
{{{< askr-image-view src="images/layout.png" label="View image" >}}}
```

Specify exactly one of `target` or `src`. Targets use the figure ID without `#`
and must identify a single eligible image on the page. `label` defaults to
`View image`; the `src` form has no caption. Paths are relative to the document.

## Inspect inline, then expand

An inline viewer supplies controls directly in the article:

```markdown
{{{< askr-image-view src="images/layout.svg" mode="inline" label="Component layout" >}}}
```

To convert an existing figure in place, preserving its caption:

```markdown
![Layout](images/layout.svg){#fig-layout}

{{{< askr-image-view target="fig-layout" mode="inline" >}}}
```

The shortcode marks the existing figure for conversion; it does not display a
second copy. Each figure can be converted once, with any number of buttons
opening it. `mode` accepts `inline` or `button` (the default).

Inline image areas are 420px high on desktop and 320px on narrow screens.
Expand moves the same viewer into a floating window. Zoom and viewing center
follow it; closing returns it to the article with the updated camera intact.
Different inline viewers have independent state. No state is saved after
leaving the page.

## Controls and galleries

- **+ / −** zoom by a factor of 1.25; **Fit** centers the whole image.
- **100%** means Fit, not original pixel size. Zooming a raster image does not
  increase its resolution. SVG may itself contain raster content.
- Drag to pan. On touchscreens use one finger to pan and two to zoom.
- Focus the inline image area before wheel zoom; otherwise the article scrolls
  normally. Floating viewers always handle wheel zoom inside their image area.
- In the focused image area, `+` / `−` zoom, `0` fits, and arrows pan.
- **Expand** opens an inline viewer; the floating toolbar has fullscreen
  (where the browser supports it) and close controls.
- Escape closes the floating viewer and restores focus and reading position.
  In browser fullscreen, Escape exits fullscreen first.

Group ordinary images into a floating gallery with the existing attribute:

```markdown
![First layout](images/first.png){group="layouts"}

![Second layout](images/second.jpg){group="layouts"}
```

Use previous/next buttons to switch; each image starts at Fit. Galleries loop
by default; `lightbox: {match: auto, loop: false}` disables looping. Expanding
an inline viewer stays on that image rather than switching away from its state.
Single-finger swipes pan; they do not change gallery images.

## Limits and migration

This replaces Askr's former GLightbox interface. Existing shortcode names,
image eligibility, captions and groups remain. GLightbox-specific `effect`,
`desc-position` and `css-class` settings are not supported; remove them before
rendering. Description text is displayed as text, never executable HTML.

Images retain their own colors in both themes. SVG is loaded as an image,
not injected into the page. This is not a GDS viewer and has no layer selection,
measurement or resolution enhancement. A failed load shows an error and Retry;
closing and gallery navigation remain available.

Without JavaScript, images and source links remain available without interactive
controls. Non-HTML output retains ordinary images and image/figure links.

Try the [Figures examples](../components/figures.qmd#image-viewer).
